text: ) is probably the current preferred treatment in high-risk pa- tients.1,2,4,5,7-9 Methotrexate, dactinomycin, and etoposide is also used.5,7 A combination of methotrexate, dactinomy- cin, and either cyclophosphamide or chlorambucil was the preferred combination in the past. Comparative studies are lacking.9 In refractory disease, the salvage regimen EMA- EP uses etoposide and cisplatin in place of cyclophospha- mide and vincristine in EMA-CO. Other regimens have used etoposide and cisplatin with either bleomycin or ifos- famide.8 Brain metastases are generally treated by local irradiation, given with chemotherapy. Modified EMA-CO, using a higher dose of systemic methotrexate and adding intrathe- cal methotrexate, is also used.7 Liver metastases have been treated with irradiation, local chemoembolisation, or sur- gical resection.2,7,8 Patients with placental site trophoblastic tumour, which is relatively insensitive to chemotherapy, may be best treated by hysterectomy in the early stages.1,2 In high-risk pa- tients, a platinum-based regimen is preferred to EMA- CO.4 1.
